  • Spider-Armor MK I: When the New Enforcers attacked New York using high caliber firearms, Spider-Man created a suite of "Spider-Armor." Composed of a pseudo-metallic compound that he developed at Empire State University, the suit slowed him down and made him less agile, but allowed him to be bulletproof. During the battle, the suit was destroyed by acid.[634]
  • Electro-Proof Suit: This suit was created by Spider-Man in order to protect himself from the villain Electro and his electricity powers in a battle alongside the X-Men against the villain.[635]
  • Anti-Magnetic Inverter: The Anti-Magnetic Inverter was a device built by Peter Parker/Spider-Man to counteract the magnetic power that the Vulture uses for flight.[163]
  • Anti-Sonic Inverter: The Anti-Sonic Inverter was a device inspired by the Anti-Magnetic Inverter and was used during his fight with Clash to erase his recording list and stop his attack.[636]
  • Ricochet's Suit: When Norman Osborn and the Trapster framed Spider-Man for murder, Peter Parker created four separate costumed identities to clear his name. The first was the Ricochet suit, which showcased his agility and had bouncing discs which were used as weapons.
  • The Hornet's Suit: The second identity used by Spider-Man to clear his name was the Hornet suit. It provided additional protection and utilized a jet pack designed by Hobie Brown, as well as sedative darts.
  • Dusk's Suit: The third identity used by Spider-Man to clear his name was the Dusk suit, which he had acquired from the Negative Zone. The suit allowed Spider-Man to blend into the shadows and fly.
  • The Prodigy's Suit: The fourth and final identity used by Spider-Man to clear his name was the Prodigy suit. It had a bulletproof vest with golden-like armor, making him appear even stronger. Due to his partially exposed face, make-up and a fake nose had to be used in order to fool people.
  • Spider-Armor MK IV: Created by Peter Parker with Parker Industries' best resources, this suit was far beyond most of his usual suits. The suit was lightweight enough that Peter could still wall-crawl with incredible ease, yet was strong enough to deflect laser shots at close range. The eyes-and-spider insignia on his chest glowed, though it is unknown if it was just for show or if it had any other purpose.[593] As of current events, Peter made this his primary suit for his missions. However, some time later, during the Secret Empire, Doctor Octopus tried to take over Parker Industries and, as part of his plan, he used a device to destroy the Spider-Armor MK IV, revealing Peter's traditional suit underneath.
  • The Clairvoyant: A device created by a student named Jamie,[637] after being exposed by the energies released by Spider-Man 2099 and being inhabited by Lyla,[638]this allowed Spider-Man to see possible probabilities of the future.[639]
  • Spider-Armor MK II: Peter created version 2.0 of his Spider-Armor to compensate for the loss of his spider-sense due to the fact that, without this ability, he could be easily wounded by bullets.[620] This suit has since been placed back in storage in Peter's office at Horizon Labs.[83] It was most likely destroyed alongside Horizon itself.[640] A replica of the suit was later stored at Parker Industries.[393]
  • Spider-Armor MK III: Created by Peter Parker with Horizon Labs' vast resources to fight the Sinister Six if needed in a last resort. When Doctor Octopus started his last master plan before dying, Spider-Man knew that he would have to use it to stop Octopus's attempt to speed up the greenhouse effect.[375] This suit has since been repaired and placed back in storage in Peter's office at Horizon Labs.[83] After Horizon Labs was destroyed,[640] Spider-Man kept the suit in his lab at Parker Industries.[393]
  • Superior Spider-Man Mark III: After his mind swap with Doctor Octopus, Peter returned to his body, got rid of Doctor Octopus's costume, and returned to his classic red and blue costume and, even further, the Mark IV Spider-Armor; yet he still could use it any time he wanted, but he chose not to. After being driven to kill by Itsy-Bitsy, and under the influence of Mephisto, he upgraded this costume even further in order to kill her. Deadpool even mentioned that he looked "kinda superiorly Doc Ock-y." Some upgrades included Spider-Arms, Laser Beams, Web Wings, and Nerve Hacking Technology. Spider-Man, however, fought against Mephisto's influence and did not kill her. Like the black costume, this one also shows Peter's dark side, which was the intention of Doctor Octopus when he created it, the costume making him appear more like a threat, which better suited him as a "hero."[588]

Transportation

  • Web-Swinging: Spider-Man uses his web-shooters to travel by swinging on web-lines. Combined with his spider-abilities, he can move at amazing speeds throughout the urban chasms of Manhattan. Spider-Man was able to keep pace with Captain Marvel at his best speed, surprising the Kree warrior, although Spider-Man mentioned it was mostly due to his practice with web-swinging over his career.[641]
Former Transportation
  • Dimensional Travel Watch: A device which allowed Spider-Man to travel through the Multiverse. It was eventually destroyed by Morlun.[642]
  • Spider-Glider: Through his resources at Horizon Labs, Spider-Man created his own version of the Goblin Glider that is used for faster travel across the city. He first used it during a fight with Equinox.[375]
  • Spider-Mobile: With his resources from Parker Industries, Peter co-created a second version of the Spider-Mobile with Lian Tang. He first used it during a fight with the Zodiac in Shanghai.[404]
  • Hydro-Spider: With his resources from Parker Industries, Peter also designed a submarine-like ship capable of going deep sea. He outfitted it with a holographic plating for stealth purposes.[593]

Notes

  • Peter became Spider-Man when he was 15 years old.[643] Since the Prime Marvel Universe operates in a sliding timescale, the period between the beginning of the Marvel Age (Fantastic Four #1, close to Spider-Man's debut in Amazing Fantasy #15) and the present is a fixed window of time of roughly 15 years. Editor Tom Brevoort stated in 2018 that Peter was 28 years old,[644] and has also acknowledged that Peter is in the same age range as other characters who have been consistently portrayed as his peers, including Jessica Jones, the Human Torch, and Cyclops.[645] However, later comics such as Amazing Spider-Man (Vol. 5) #14 from 2019 have described him as being in his mid-20s instead.
    • In Amazing Spider-Man (Vol. 3) #1, it is stated that 13 years have passed since he was bitten by a spider at the age of 15, and a similar description appears in Peter Parker: The Spectacular Spider-Man Annual #1, which supports the fact that he is 28 years old.
    • However, in Amazing Spider-Man: Spider-Versity #1, Cindy Moon, who is close in age to Peter, is stated to be mid-20s, seemingly supporting the age estimate from Amazing Spider-Man (Vol. 5) #14.
    • It should be noted that Johnny Storm and Cyclops are actually a year or two older than Peter, as Peter was 15 during the time of Amazing Fantasy #15 and his first few issues, Johnny Storm was said to be 16 at the time of his first appearance,[646] which is set before Peter became Spider-Man, and Cyclops was approximately 17 during his own.[647]
  • The only person killed by Spider-Man is Charlemagne. Even though it was unintentional, this accident continued to haunt him later on in his life.[494]
  • Peter was married to Mary Jane Watson prior to the alteration of his personal history by Mephisto, who did this in order to prevent the couple's daughter from being born and threaten to overthrow his inevitable rule on Earth.[340][157] However, despite this, Peter and Mary Jane rekindled their relationship,[423] and he was planning to propose to her again.[648] They even moved back in together after the fall of the Beyond Corporation,[159] but their relationship was again broken, as Peter had been alienated from everyone he cared about. Despite this, he has shown that he wants to get back with her, but cannot for now because Mary Jane is in another relationship.
  • The following is an approximate list of living people that know Spider-Man's secret identity: Mary Jane Watson,[649] the Jackal, Kaine, Ben Reilly, Spidercide, Mephisto,[140] the entire roster of the New Avengers during Norman Osborn's reign (Luke Cage, Iron Fist, Captain Marvel, the Mockingbird, Hawkeye, Spider-Woman, Jessica Jones, Wolverine, Doctor Strange, and the Winter Soldier),[346] Danielle Cage,[346] the Fantastic Four (Mister Fantastic, the Invisible Woman, the Thing, and the Human Torch),[650] Franklin Richards,[651] N'Kalla Masters-Grimm,[652] the Order of the Web (Madame Web, Silk,[653] Miles Morales, the Ghost-Spider,[397] and Anya Corazón[654]), Carlie Cooper,[571] Captain America,[655] Flag-Smasher, Mysterio,[387] Anna Maria Marconi,[393] Teresa Parker,[412] Karnak the Shatterer,[656] Gwenpool,[657] J. Jonah Jameson,[418] Loki,[658] the Master Matrix,[659] Norman Osborn,[419] the Venom symbiote and Eddie Brock,[422] Normie Osborn,[422] Flash Thompson,[422] Dylan Brock,[434][660] the Black Cat,[661] the Rumor,[662] Moon Girl,[663] Hallow's Eve,[3] Marcus Momplaisir,[159] the Ultra Living Brain,[38] Crystal Catawnee,[664] the Queen Goblin,[665] Spider-Boy,[144] Rek-Rap,[29] Paul Rabin,[451] Anansi,[666] Thor,[667] Emma Frost,[668] Ms. Marvel,[474] Re-Po,[669] Nightcrawler,[670] the Crime Lord,[671] Weapon X-31,[672] Kate Bishop, Jeff the Land Shark,[673] Xanto Starblood, Rocket Raccoon, Raelith, Nial, Symbie,[31] the Carnage symbiote,[674] Daredevil,[542] Mac Crane,[675] and Spider-Girl.[676]
    • This list does not count all the refugees from the Ultimate Universe who may or may not also know his secret identity, such as Ganke Lee and Miles' parents, Rio and Jeff.[677][678]
      • While Miguel O'Hara and various other members of the Multiversal Spider-Army know that Peter Parker is the original Spider-Man,[679] they are not included since they are neither from, nor currently residing in, the Prime Marvel Universe.
    • This list also does not include beings with inherent abilities that would tell them who Spider-Man is, such as Lady Sif.[667]
    • Peter seems to be unaware of the fact that Thor knows his secret identity.[680]
    • The Stonethrower was able to discern Peter's civilian alter-ego from Spider-Man, but is not actually acquainted with Peter Parker nor knows his name.[681]
    • Elsa Bloodstone[682] and the Last Son of Kraven[160] have both seen Spider-Man unmasked, but it is unknown if either of them actually know his secret identity.
    • Robbie Thompson, the writer of Spider-Man/Deadpool, wanted Deadpool to learn Spider-Man's secret identity; however, Marvel Comics would not allow that. So, in the final story arc of the series, Thompson created an "event," with himself as the main villain, the Manipulator, in order for Marvel to allow Deadpool to learn Spider-Man's identity. In the end that did not happen, as Spider-Man and Deadpool put the Manipulator in jail.[683]
    • During Absolute Carnage, when Cletus Kasady was impersonating Eddie Brock and talking to an unsuspecting Spider-Man, the actual Eddie tried to warn Peter, but unintentionally revealed to Kasady Spider-Man's first name as "Pete."[684]
    • Mystique, Warlock, and one of Legion's subpersonalities spied on a conversation between Spider-Man and the Creepy Crawler, overhearing Kurt calling him "Peter."[670]
  • It has been shown that those with telepathic abilities, such as Chamber, can sense Peter's spider-sense when it is activated by danger and that (with some difficulty) by linking their minds together, his spider-sense can be telepathically broadcasted to those around him in order to allow them to sense the same danger that he does.[685]
  • Allegedly, Peter had heard that his school's dance team were throwing out old bodysuits, so he sneaked into school after dark, found one that fit him, obtained two two-way mirrors from the Drama Department's prop closet (for his mask's eye lenses) and spent an hour silk screening the web pattern onto the bodysuit in the art room. With this, he created his first Spider-Man costume.[538]
  • Despite Peter being officially and consistently classified with gifted intelligence,[56][5][4] he once claimed to possess an IQ north of 250.[686] For reference, in the real world, the person with the highest recorded IQ score is allegedly Ainan Celeste Cawley (263),[687] and in the Ultimate Universe, Reed Richards has an IQ of 267.[688]
  • Regarding his ability to climb walls, Peter normally needs to take off his shoes or any kind of thick footwear; however, he is sometimes drawn being able to climb with his shoes on. According to Marvel editor Tom Brevoort: "Shoes off is correct. Shoes on is a mistake made so often it became faux-right."[689]

Creation[]

  • Jack Kirby has claimed to have created Spider-Man and have given the character to Steve Ditko.[690]
    • This may tie in to an alleged "cover-up" which stated that Steve Ditko, when designing Spider-Man, was partially inspired by Ben Cooper Halloween Costume's Spiderman costume, which predates Spider-Man,[691] and according to some alleged sources, Jack Kirby used to work for the Ben Cooper company, designing their costumes.[692]
  • Steve Ditko originally envisioned Spider-Man's costume as orange and purple. Ditko has assumed that it was changed to red and blue either due to the printing limitations of the era or because Marvel thought red and blue was more striking.[693]
  • During Steve Ditko's time on the series The Amazing Spider-Man, when shooting webs Spider-Man only stuck out his thumb and pointing finger minus the pinky finger. Because Steve Ditko used to draw the characters with their pinky finger sticking out, this caused Spider-Man to also stick out his pinky fingers when shooting webs.[694]
    • Spider-Man shares this hand gesture with Doctor Strange, who was also co-created by Steve Ditko; this was also acknowledged by the characters themselves in Spider-Man: Fever #3.
  • It is revealed in Excelsior! The Amazing Life of Stan Lee, that Spider-Man was based on the Spider (Richard Wentworth), despite Lee stating that he was inspired by a fly walking on a wall.[695]
  • When Stan Lee first pitched the idea of Spider-Man, his publisher, Martin Goodman, was at first against it, since people hated spiders. This is why Spider-Man made his debut in Amazing Fantasy #15, since the Amazing Adult Fantasy series was planned to be cancelled anyway.[695]
    • This may actually tie to the fact that Spider-Man was allegedly going to be portrayed as a horror comic, since according to Horror Comics: The Illustrated History, Steve Ditko was famous for drawing horror comics, and this can be witnessed in Spider-Man's first appearance as he was drawn with a horror atmosphere, which Stan Lee liked.[696] The connection was also acknowledged in Gerry Conway's book Webslinger: Unauthorized Essays on Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man.

"With Great Power Comes Great Responsibility"[]

  • Spider-Man's famous mantra "with great power comes great responsibility" is often attributed as a quote from Uncle Ben; however, it was originally the concluding lines of narration to his first appearance in Amazing Fantasy #15, the anonymous narrator explaining the moral of the story, not advice from his beloved uncle. As this was the lesson he had learned from his uncle's death, it slowly became associated with Uncle Ben, and the 2002 film chose to have the famous phrase come directly from Ben Parker as advice to the newly-powered Peter, and this is how the origin of the phrase is commonly understood now.
  • The quote "With great power comes great responsibility" was first used by Peter in a comic book in 1987, Spider-Man Versus Wolverine #1. It is mentioned as a saying of Uncle Ben's in that issue, though it was not spoken by him. The first time Ben actually said it in a comic was in February 2002, in Amazing Spider-Man (Vol. 2) #38; meanwhile, in 2016's Amazing Spider-Man & Silk: The Spider(fly) Effect Infinite Comic #4, Ben tells Peter that the phrase originated with his father, Peter's paternal grandfather.

Trivia

  • Nick Fury's intelligence classified Spider-Man as power level 8.[105]
  • Peter Parker has sometimes not worn any underwear beneath his Spider-Man suit.[697]
  • After being attached to Ms. Marvel, Venom stated that she had feelings for Spider-Man.[698]
  • Before her supposed death, Silver Sable also appeared to have feelings for Spider-Man.[699]
  • Spider-Man and Wolverine became blood brothers during a time-travel adventure.[700]
  • Peter seemingly dislikes mayonnaise, at least in sandwiches, and prefers those with free-crust.[701]
  • Peter is a lifelong fan of the New York Mets.[702]
  • Peter has learned to speak Mandarin.[404]
  • Though Spider-Man has claimed to hate Star Wars,[703] he sometimes references it.[704][705]
  • Spider-Man is familiar with the Lord of the Rings franchise.[706]
  • After years of busting thieves and cat burglars, Peter has picked up on how to pick locks. He was also given a set of lock picks from the Black Cat.[707]
  • In his first appearance in Amazing Fantasy #15, the spider that bit Parker was mistakenly called an insect.
  • S.H.I.E.L.D. managed to reverse-engineer Spider-Man's web formula many years ago according to Buck Lime, the Moon Knight's assistant, who built web-shooters for him.[708]
  • Several times, Spider-Man has been mistaken as a mutant. At one point, J. Jonah Jameson actually sent him to X-Factor for confirmation,[709] and at another, he was hunted down by Magneto until the misunderstanding was corrected.[710]
  • It has been implied that Peter has trademarked the Spider-Man motif after mobilizing Parker Industries.[711][712] This was later revealed to be true, as the Beyond Corporation had bought the trademark of Spider-Man from the now-defunct company.[158]
  • Peter has both a Twitter[713] and a Facebook account.[714] While the Superior Spider-Man used a Skype account under Peter's name, it is unknown if Peter himself has ever used the account.[623]
  • Canonically, Peter is a Libra because his birthday is on September 23.[404]
  • Spider-Man considers Five Guys to have the best hamburgers in New York.[715]
  • Peter's locker combination in middle school was 06-18-28.[659]
  • Peter's favorite breakfast is wheat cakes.[2]
  • Marvel writers are allegedly forbidden from having scenes that show Peter Parker drinking beer.[716]
  • Peter is the godfather of Normie Osborn.[422]
  • Peter Parker's ringtone for J. Jonah Jameson's phone calls is Run-DMC's song "You Talk Too Much".[717]
  • When Peter began living with Fred Myers and Randy Robertson, their apartment's number was 616.[434]
  • Spider-Man has visited Tim Harrison,[533] and Nathan,[718] two of his biggest young fans who were suffering from cancer. He was also saddened when he found out that Fusion's son had died when trying to emulate him.[719]
  • Norman Osborn sees Peter as his ideal son, and even deemed him worthy to be the heir to the identity of the Green Goblin.[720]
  • Peter is a distant cousin to the Beezer family through his Aunt May, including Gus Beezer and Tillie Beezer; due to these being joke characters from a kid's comedy series with questionable placement in canon, these relations have never appeared outside of Gus Beezer comics, such as Marvelous Adventures of Gus Beezer: Spider-Man #1 and Marvelous Adventures of Gus Beezer: Gus Beezer & Spider-Man #1
  • In Absolute Carnage: Breakout, Spider-Man was voiced by Cole Howard.
  • Peter believes that if Gwen had survived, he never would have ended up with Mary Jane, and has been haunted by this belief ever since.[721] However, Mary Jane has a firm belief that she and Peter are destined to be together.[340] This would later be confirmed at the end of the Kindred Saga, where after Doctor Strange freed Peter's soul from Mephisto's influence and discovered his motivations in wanting to separate him from MJ, he reiterated that the devil's actions ended up only making the couple's connection unbreakable.[340][157]
  • Since Doctor Strange died before he managed to reveal to Peter about Mephisto's interference in his life, both he and Mary Jane are still unaware of their deal with the devil.[722] Ironically, just when Doctor Strange was finally resurrected, Peter ended up being killed and erased from reality, once again preventing him from finding out about his deal with the devil.
  • Peter has stated that purchasing the chemicals he uses to manufacture his web-fluid costs around 2,000 dollars.[109]
  • Peter finds Miles Morales' black and red costume cooler than his own.[384]
  • Peter keeps caches of spare clothes hidden all over New York City.[723]
  • Supercharger is canonically the first costumed villain Spider-Man has faced.[724]
  • Peter gained the powers of the Hulk and became the Spider-Hulk three times.[15][16][17]
  • Peter's contact name in Cindy Moon's phone was "P💩P."[725]
  • Peter had a habit of not opening his emails.[119]
  • Silk is Peter's favorite organic fiber.[68]
  • In Fortnite, Spider-Man was mysteriously brought to Reality Zero's Artemis island, alongside the Daily Bugle Building.[726] There, he joined forces with The Seven to help defeat both the Imagined Order and Doctor Doom.[727] Later on, he helps The Underground defeat Doctor Doom on the Helios island.[728]
  • Spider-Man once met the Joker, a super-villain from New Earth in the DC Universe.[729] Later Ben Reilly, who had assumed the identity of Spider-Man at that time, met the Joker as well, with the latter saying to him "Spider-Man, I presume, but you've changed costumes since last we fought.", not knowing at all that this Spider-Man was a clone of the original one. Ben started to tell the Joker that he did not know what he was talking about before the Joker interrupted him.[730]
  • Spider-Man's favorite TV show is the real life talk show Comedy Bang! Bang!,[731] and one of his favorite films ever is the fictional Fast Car Family Five.[732]
  • In Marvel's Squirrel Girl: The Unbeatable Radio Show!, Spider-Man was voiced by Paul Scheer.
